key_points.description: Purpose of the meeting: align Bennett Contracting, DataSkate, and MuleSoft on integration scope, approach, and pricing for connecting Sage 100 Contractor with Salesforce.
Bennett is using Sage 100 Contractor (version 2026, 1.158.0) hosted on a Windows Server in Azure, with EI Dynamics currently handling integration between Sage and Salesforce.
Sage 100 Contractor does not provide direct REST APIs; DataSkate's approach involves either custom .NET wrappers over ODBC/BOIs or third-party APIs to enable read/write data exchange with MuleSoft.
Agreed integration scope — Salesforce to Sage: customer/account creation and updates, and order creation; Sage to Salesforce: change orders, invoice creation, and payment-received updates.
SharePoint-to-Sage purchase order integration was confirmed as in scope; updates to existing POs are handled by creating a new PO rather than modifying the original.
WorkMax was explicitly excluded from scope, as it has its own background integration software.
DataSkate quoted $18,000 and 8–9 weeks for full implementation, covering requirements gathering, development, testing, UAT, and production deployment.
Two weeks of post-go-live hypercare support is included, covering monitoring, issue resolution, and knowledge transfer to Bennett's team.
Beyond hypercare, DataSkate offers two support models: monthly managed services with a dedicated developer, or a retainer bucket-of-hours with a ~2-day turnaround.
Rob confirmed MuleSoft/Salesforce has additional customer success levers available in FY27 to assist if integration issues arise on their end.
Mike Britton expressed hesitancy based on past experience with Sage 100 integrations always running over time and cost, and not always working reliably.
DataSkate proposed a recorded demo of their in-progress Sage 300 CRe integration to build confidence, with a live demo possible pending client approval.
Mike Britton requested client references from DataSkate — ideally from similar industries — to speak with before committing.
Kailash committed to providing references and a recorded Sage 300 CRe demo by Friday, with a live demo to follow if client approval is obtained.
Follow-up meeting scheduled for Monday, June 29th at 10:00 AM to reconvene after Mike reviews the demo and speaks with references.

**MuleSoft  Bennett Contracting Implementation Conversation with DataSkate**
🕞 Started at 02:59 PM on 15 Jun, lasted 37m
data.raw_content:
## Action Items
- [ ]  Kailash to share a couple of client references that Mike could talk to about integration work.  - kailash chanda - Due: 06/20/2026
- [ ]  Kailash to provide an update on when a recorded demo of the Sage 300 CRE connectivity can be shared.  - kailash chanda - Due: 06/20/2026
- [ ]  Kailash to seek client approval for a live demo of the Sage 300 CRE integration.  - kailash chanda
- [ ]  Rob to send a calendar invite for Monday June 29th at 10:00 AM.  - Due: 06/29/2026
- [ ]  Rob to make introductions to reference customers as required. 

## Key Points
- Purpose of the meeting: align Bennett Contracting, DataSkate, and MuleSoft on integration scope, approach, and pricing for connecting Sage 100 Contractor with Salesforce. 
- Bennett is using Sage 100 Contractor (version 2026, 1.158.0) hosted on a Windows Server in Azure, with EI Dynamics currently handling integration between Sage and Salesforce. 
- Sage 100 Contractor does not provide direct REST APIs; DataSkate's approach involves either custom .NET wrappers over ODBC/BOIs or third-party APIs to enable read/write data exchange with MuleSoft. 
- Agreed integration scope — Salesforce to Sage: customer/account creation and updates, and order creation; Sage to Salesforce: change orders, invoice creation, and payment-received updates. 
- SharePoint-to-Sage purchase order integration was confirmed as in scope; updates to existing POs are handled by creating a new PO rather than modifying the original. 
- WorkMax was explicitly excluded from scope, as it has its own background integration software. 
- DataSkate quoted $18,000 and 8–9 weeks for full implementation, covering requirements gathering, development, testing, UAT, and production deployment. 
- Two weeks of post-go-live hypercare support is included, covering monitoring, issue resolution, and knowledge transfer to Bennett's team. 
- Beyond hypercare, DataSkate offers two support models: monthly managed services with a dedicated developer, or a retainer bucket-of-hours with a ~2-day turnaround. 
- Rob confirmed MuleSoft/Salesforce has additional customer success levers available in FY27 to assist if integration issues arise on their end. 
- Mike Britton expressed hesitancy based on past experience with Sage 100 integrations always running over time and cost, and not always working reliably. 
- DataSkate proposed a recorded demo of their in-progress Sage 300 CRe integration to build confidence, with a live demo possible pending client approval. 
- Mike Britton requested client references from DataSkate — ideally from similar industries — to speak with before committing. 
- Kailash committed to providing references and a recorded Sage 300 CRe demo by Friday, with a live demo to follow if client approval is obtained. 
- Follow-up meeting scheduled for Monday, June 29th at 10:00 AM to reconvene after Mike reviews the demo and speaks with references.
